items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Nicki plays bari sax [error, Nicki plays bass and Lisa plays bari sax] in our big band... I love playing with Nicki. I think she’s one of the best bass players I know.

ctx.x: And I couldn’t figure out what was going on for a minute. I thought I knew what song this was and then it shifted and I’m going that was really neat. Wasn’t your tenor player playing in that set I think? © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

Yeah, Anat. An interesting thing, since you mentioned Anat is also what I’m finding really fascinating is well I’m the only American in my quintet first of all. But the women in Diva are literally women from all over the world. That’s really fascinating also, how our alto player, Karolina Strassmayer comes from Bad Mitterndorf, Austria, this little tiny village. Her dad is like a forest ranger. You know how the heck did she come out playing — like an unbelievable jazz player. She a genius, a brilliant jazz…

That’s interesting. If this was an all-guy band and you had those same nationalities they would probably promote it as an international type band. But you’ve got two kinds of interesting identities to your band. It’s great.
